messages.author: 9160793b546521df
messages.subject: BMA with NIMBLE
parts:
Hello, 

I am interested in doing BMA and I have done some reading and researching online about calculating weights for the different posterior samples. I think what could be compatible with nimble as an approach would be to caclualte the log marginal likelihood see here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bridgesampling/vignettes/bridgesampling_example_nimble.html

and use the log marginal likelihood to weight the posterior samples. I have also read about stacking to average predictive distributions and psuedo-bma (AIC-type of weighting but im not sure how proper is to create weights based on the WAIC which is readily available in NIMBLE), see here:

https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bayesian-analysis/volume-13/issue-3/Using-Stacking-to-Average-Bayesian-Predictive-Distributions-with-Discussion/10.1214/17-BA1091.full

Is there any relevant literature or tutorials for BMA in nimble? Any ideas?

Best wishes, 
Gary

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: BMA with NIMBLE
parts:
hi Gary,

We don't have any specific tools for this in NIMBLE. You can of course write nimbleFunctions to implement various methods, though normalizing constant methods are not always easy to implement.

-chris
